CURRENT PRODUCTION FUNCTION
Q = P½S½

How to read elasticity and isoquants

σ measures the percentage change in the input ratio S/P associated with a 1% change in the marginal rate of technical substitution, along an isoquant. It describes the flexibility of the technology, not its overall productivity.

With P on the horizontal axis, an isoquant’s slope is −MPP/MPS. Its absolute value is the amount of suppression that one extra unit of preparedness can replace locally, holding output fixed.

For finite σ > 0, the CES function uses ρ = (σ − 1)/σ. Cobb–Douglas is the limit at σ = 1. The endpoint presets show the exact limiting functions.
